mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies adjust to lower revenue expectations.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS drops > 2% YoY, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected contraction in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production delays and increased costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO drops > 1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing market boosts economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) inflation is rising, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase significantly (> 200k MoM) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 200k MoM and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% YoY and Industrial Production (INDPRO) also declines, it signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% YoY and INDPRO declines
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth < 1% YoY and INDPRO declines, the hypothesis is rejected.
